text:
Raj: FYI, just hit a weird one — several GPU nodes in us-west-2 show Ready but pods can't reach external services, health checks from the NLB failing :confused:
Ashley: Are these new nodes or an edge config change?
Raj: Rolling pools, but only the new pool (gpu-pool-4) is affected. Old pools healthy.
Sofia: Any errors in kube-proxy or iptables?
Raj: Saw a bunch of conntrack drops and tcp reset logs. Kube-proxy shows endpoints present, but NLB TargetGroup mark_unhealthy with TCP reset.
Raj: Quick debug commands I ran:
```
kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep gpu-pool-4
kubectl describe node ip-10-0-132-45.us-west-2.compute.internal
sudo conntrack -L | tail -n 50
```
Ashley: Could be ephemeral port range or NACL blocking ephemeral >1024. Anything changed on VPC ACLs?
Raj: I checked the NACLs — looks like the subnet attached to new pool has a policy that only allows TCP 443 and 1024-2048 outbound, denies everything else.
Oncall-SRE: That explains it — AWS NACLs are stateless, so both inbound and outbound need ephemeral ports open for return traffic from external services.
Sofia: How did that NACL end up on the subnet? Did terraform apply target the wrong subnet id?
Raj: Yep. terraform var for subnet_map.us-west-2 had an extra entry, new pool got spun into a sandbox subnet with restrictive NACL copied from a security-sensitive project.
Ashley: Can we patch quickly? Suggest two options:
 1) Modify NACL to allow ephemeral ports (1024-65535) outbound and corresponding inbound established ports.
 2) Move ASG to the correct subnet (riskier during traffic).
Oncall-SRE: Modify NACL is lower blast radius. I'll prepare change and run through safety checks.
infra-bot: Deploy window scheduled at 2026-06-09T22:30Z for NACL updates (change-id: nacl-allow-ephemeral-1769).
Sofia: Also check the SGs attached to the nodes — if they reference a prefix-list or a wrong service CIDR that could block LB health checks.
Raj: SGs look fine (allow 0.0.0.0/0 443, 10250 for kubelet). This is definitely subnet NACL.
Ashley: Postfix: remind infra team to not copy-reuse restrictive NACLs across sandbox->prod. Maybe add a terraform guardrail to prevent attaching 'sensitive' NACL to pools tagged env=prod.
Oncall-SRE: NACL updated: allowed ephemeral (1024-65535) outbound and ephemeral inbound for established responses. Monitoring: target group healthy count increasing.
Raj: Seeing recovery — health checks passing now :tada: Pods that were failing external calls are succeeding.
Sofia: Good catch. Can we add an automated check in provisioning to compare intended subnet tags vs applied NACL?
Ashley: +1. I'll open a quick ticket for a pre-provisioning policy and a post-provision smoke test (curl to external public IP from a test pod).
infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-4321 "prevent restrictive NACLs on prod GPU subnets".
Raj: Thanks all. Leaving a note in the pool terraform module to warn about NACLs and include the smoke test.
Ashley: Optional: add ephemeral port assertion to the CIS/networking checklist.
Sofia: Closing loop: root cause = wrong subnet selection in terraform var -> restrictive NACL (ephemeral ports blocked) -> NLB target health failures and GPU pod egress failures.
Raj: Tagging ops for postmortem follow-up and cost impact check (some retries spiked egress costs slightly).
Oncall-SRE: Will draft a short postmortem and list remediation steps.
Ashley: Great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
